title: Godot 4 (GDScript) → Unity (C#)
conventions: One GDScript file becomes one C# MonoBehaviour (class name = file name in PascalCase; Unity requires the class name to match the file name).
A .tscn scene becomes a prefab; the main scene becomes a Unity scene. Child nodes become child GameObjects; a node's own type (CharacterBody3D, Area3D…) becomes components on that GameObject.

Coordinates: Godot is right-handed with -Z forward, Unity is left-handed with +Z forward. Mirror Z: position (x, y, -z), quaternion (-x, -y, z, w). Use port_convert; meshes imported separately keep their own importer orientation.
Godot angles are radians (rotation), Unity Euler angles are degrees (eulerAngles). Physics ticks: Godot 60 Hz, Unity 50 Hz by default (Time.fixedDeltaTime = 0.02).
Prefer serialized references ([SerializeField]) over path lookups; wire them in the prefab instead of get_node paths.
Unity has no per-node 'process' toggle like set_process; disable the component (enabled = false) or the GameObject.

entries.to: public class X : MonoBehaviour
entries.notes: The Godot base type (CharacterBody3D, Area3D, RigidBody3D…) is not the C# base class: add the matching components (CharacterController, Collider+isTrigger, Rigidbody) to the GameObject.

entries.to: Awake() for self-setup, Start() when other objects must exist
entries.notes: Godot runs children's _ready before the parent's; Unity's Awake/Start order between objects is not guaranteed (use Script Execution Order if it matters).

entries.notes: Default rates differ (60 vs 50 Hz); set Project Settings → Time → Fixed Timestep to 1/60 to keep tuning.
